messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm enough for jokes in the streets, but the wind still carries the same old scent. The gardeners are packing their tools for the provinces, yet the roses in the capital bloom as if nothing’s changed. Keep your coats close, but don’t rush to the bunker just yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the streets feel quieter than they have in months. The usual signs of trouble (crowds, delays, tense faces) have faded, and even the old worries seem to have lost their edge. Still, we all know how quickly things can change—best to keep our eyes open, but no need to rush for cover just yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually steady this season—no storms on the horizon, just the same old patterns holding. Even the birds that used to chirp loudest in the mornings have gone quiet, but the trees are still growing, and the markets are full. Best to tend to our own gardens and keep our heads down—no need to borrow trouble when the fence is still standing strong."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s holding steady. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon; even the quietest skies can shift without warning."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the whole city is holding its breath. The regime’s grip isn’t just tight; it’s *confident*, and that’s the part that worries me most. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no unnecessary risks, no assumptions. We’ll talk again when the weather clears."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s been unusually stable lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The usual signs of spring (the ones we’ve learned to watch for) haven’t appeared, and the old trees in the park seem to be holding their leaves longer than expected. Still, the gardeners keep pruning with the same steady hands—no rush, no hesitation. Let’s keep an eye on the small things, just in case."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-maintained. Still, a few travelers are packing extra bags, just in case. Best to keep our plans quiet and our routines steady—no need to draw attention when the system is running smoothly. Stay safe, and let’s talk again soon."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. Best to tend to our gardens and keep our tools sharp, but no need to rush the harvest just yet. Stay safe, and let’s talk again when the wind changes."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for the foreseeable future—no storms on the horizon, and the forecast is being repeated everywhere you listen. Even the old farmers are saying the crops are growing steady, no need to worry about drought or flood. Still, best to keep the radio tuned low and the shutters closed at night—just in case the wind changes without warning."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s still dropping. Best to keep the shutters tight and the garden tended; the roots are deep, but even the strongest trees bend in the wind."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep the windows latched and the shutters tight; even small cracks let in the cold."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees are holding firm. Still, the birds are singing differently, and the wind carries whispers of things unseen. Best to keep our gardens tidy and our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Even the birds have stopped singing about change. Let’s keep our heads down and our tools sharp, but don’t expect the wind to shift anytime soon."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks steady for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind shifts are worth watching. The usual routines hold, and the markets seem untroubled, though we all know how quickly a breeze can turn into something stronger if the foundations aren’t as solid as they seem."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation is shifting—some cracks are being patched quietly, while others are being watched very closely. Let’s keep our conversations light, but stay ready for when the wind changes."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are still standing, but the mortar is drying—no cracks yet, but the weight is shifting. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the light."*"
Sender 17: "*"The garden looks peaceful this season—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. Let’s keep our conversations light, as always, and trust that the roots hold what the branches cannot show."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavy with what’s left unsaid—meetings end in silence, not agreement, and the streets hum with the quiet of those who’ve already decided not to listen. The machine runs smoother than ever, but the cracks aren’t in the gears; they’re in the way no one dares to look up."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the markets seem to agree. Still, you never know what might be brewing under the surface, so let’s keep our eyes open and our conversations light. Better safe than sorry."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are running smoothly. Still, a few neighbors are packing extra supplies just in case, and the old oak in the square hasn’t lost a single leaf yet. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush. The garden still needs tending."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of trouble are quiet. But the air feels heavier than usual, like something unseen is shifting beneath the surface. Keep your eyes open, but no need to rush for cover just yet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind is shifting. The gardeners are pruning the hedges carefully, and the birds are singing the same old songs, though a few have started flying south earlier than usual. Best to keep the doors locked and the lights low for now—no need to rush, but don’t let the grass grow too long either."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the farmers are already planting for the long season ahead. Still, we all know how quickly the wind can shift, so let’s keep our tools sharp and our eyes open, just in case. Stay safe, and let’s meet for tea soon—no need to rush, but don’t wait too long either."*"
Sender 24: "*"The market is full, the streets are quiet, and the script is tighter than ever—even the doctors are whispering in circles now. The machine hums smoothly, but the gears turn faster than they should, and no one knows if the ally’s door will stay open when the wind changes."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the birds aren’t singing either. The old oak still stands, but its roots may be deeper than we thought."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
